Patchwork CI is now running on 1,200 repositories, about 900 of them open source. 💚

When we launched, we promised Patchwork CI would always be free for open source. Many people told us we were crazy. "How will you make money?" they asked.

Across those repositories, 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test. That's countless hours of developer time spent on red builds that weren't real failures.

Open source has given us users, data, feedback, and a community. OSS maintainers asked for GitLab support more than any other feature, and we shipped it on November 12. 🚀

Giving back is part of our strategy.

#OpenSource #DevOps #CI #DeveloperExperience #BuildInPublic

1,000 families. 💛

Today, 1,000 families pay €4.99 a month to make dinner time a little easier.

We got here without fancy ad campaigns or growth hacks. Most families found us through school WhatsApp groups, where parents recommended us to other parents. That trust means a lot. 🙏

#Startups #Portugal #Parenting #FemaleFounders #Gratitude

We built a beautiful app for Rotaship. In the first month, only 12% of restaurant staff opened it.

We were proud of its sleek, modern design and thought staff would love it. But the app was adding a problem rather than solving one: restaurant teams already used WhatsApp and didn't want another app.

In 2025, we made the tough call to move everything into WhatsApp. Rotaship now has 140 outlets, and the median reply time to shift messages is under 20 minutes.

We had to let go of something we loved and meet users where they already were.

#ProductManagement #Indonesia #StartupLessons #UserExperience

After 11 years in a clinic, I walked away.

I’ve always loved being a vet, but it broke my heart to see anxious pets so terrified that we had to sedate them just to examine them.

In September, we raised Tabwise's price by 50%, from $8 to $12 per user per month. It was one of the scariest decisions in our history.

Our support costs per customer had doubled since launch. We could compromise on quality or charge what we felt we were worth. We raised the price.

Customers pay for outcomes, not just software. Don't be afraid to price accordingly.

#SaaS #Pricing #StartupLessons #Growth #B2B

Our first production run at Shelfwise didn't go as planned: 400 labels shipped with a faulty battery contact.

We also introduced a 100% contact test at the factory. Since then, we've had zero contact failures across 6,000 labels.

To other hardware founders: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they don't happen again.

#Hardware #Startups #Manufacturing #Leadership #Integrity

Why we walked away from the 25% recruiting fee

For years, Northbound Talent charged 25% of a hire's first-year salary, as recruiting firms do.

Our average fee was about $41,000 per hire. For an early-stage startup, that's a massive chunk of runway. The percentage also meant we'd earn more if the salary was higher, which never felt right to me.

In January, we switched to a flat $18,000 per hire.

This year, we've placed 26 senior Rust engineers, and our client relationships have never been stronger.

I think the recruiting industry needs to evolve. Founders deserve better.

Localizing your SaaS for the Baltics and Nordics? Here are a few things to watch for:

1/ Estonian has 14 grammatical cases. One word can take many forms, and your UI needs to accommodate them.

2/ In our projects, Finnish strings are about 30% longer than English strings on average. That can make a button label hard to fit.

3/ The #1 bug we fix is hard-coded button widths. At Linguo Labs, we review every translation inside your running app so we can see it in context.
